- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or 2–5 points if spike occurred.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–3% or 2–5 points, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often underestimates sharp upward moves (e.g., 70→75+), especially after positive sentiment; apply “overshoot correction” by adding 2–5 points to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 and price > 70.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion: if sentiment is neutral or negative and price is above 70, forecast should be slightly lower than model; if below 65, slightly higher.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early momentum; if sentiment is positive and price is rising, add 1–2 points to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to be flat; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to adjust forecast direction.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 75→80) is common; if sentiment is positive after spike, reduce forecast by 2–5 points for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
